advice: Propose a fused blocked transpose-and-pack experiment for the existing general-size SME fallback. In gemm, allocate one temporary buffer and fill it directly in the packed layout consumed by the FP32 outer-product kernel, replacing the separate full A transpose followed by reads of the transposed matrix. Define each packed tile explicitly; for the current kernel, store Aᵀ values so the address for reduction index k and output-row lane i matches the kernel’s existing `at[k*n+i]` access. Keep B and C layouts, arithmetic order, tile traversal, ABI, and fallback behavior unchanged. Compare this against the current transpose-plus-consume path across every supported n, including tails and n<=0, with allocation failure falling back safely. This is a distinct layout/conversion experiment; its expected effect is unknown.
risks: The kernel currently consumes a dense transpose, so a packed layout may require changing its loads or may only move work rather than remove it. Fusing conversion with packing can change traversal and cache behavior, and one fixed tile may not suit all sizes. Any temporary allocation and conversion remain timed. Validate full output overwrite, fresh inputs, numerical tolerance 0.002, general-size boundaries, tails, allocation failure, and repeated paired controls under unchanged settings. Do not infer benefit without measurements or attribute a joint outcome to this advisor.
